details.description: GPT-5.6 Luna is the cost-efficient tier of OpenAI's GPT-5.6 family, launched July 9, 2026 alongside the flagship Sol and mid-tier Terra, aimed at cost-sensitive, high-volume workloads. OpenAI later made it the default model for Free and Go ChatGPT users, reporting about 62% fewer responses with at least one factual error than the prior default on financial, medical and legal test prompts. OpenAI has since launched a newer GPT-6 family (Astra, Sol, Luna) on September 22, 2026, and its current API model documentation no longer lists GPT-5.6 Luna among its featured models, though the catalog's own deprecation date for this model is not until January 2028.
advantages: OpenAI reports about 62% fewer responses with at least one factual error than the prior default ChatGPT model, tested on financial, medical and legal prompts.
Reaches 74.6 on OpenAI's Coding Agent Index score, per OpenAI's launch page.
Supports reasoning effort from none through max plus tool use (web search, file search, code interpreter, computer use, MCP), per OpenAI's API documentation.
Designed for cost-sensitive, high-volume workloads as the fastest, most cost-efficient tier of the GPT-5.6 family, per OpenAI's model documentation.
disadvantages: Lowest-scoring tier of the GPT-5.6 family on OpenAI's own launch benchmarks, e.g. 48.9% on SEC-Bench Pro and 45.6% on OSWorld 2.0, versus Sol's 71.2% and 62.6%.
Superseded by GPT-6 Luna, part of the GPT-6 family OpenAI launched September 22, 2026; OpenAI's current model documentation no longer features GPT-5.6 among its lineup.
Text output only; knowledge cutoff of February 16, 2026, per OpenAI's model documentation.
use_cases: High-volume, cost-sensitive chat and everyday conversational tasks
Free-tier ChatGPT default assistant, with a 'Think' toggle for harder questions
Lightweight agentic workflows and tool-calling at lower cost than Sol or Terra

notes: openai.com/index pages returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch; content was retrieved through a read-only fetch proxy. Catalog's max_input_tokens facts list two values (922,000 and 1,000,000) across snapshots/hosts and max_output_tokens 128,000; kept as-is rather than restated as one number. Catalog carries a deprecation_date of 2028-01-11 for this target, well after the September 2026 GPT-6 launch -- described as superseded in OpenAI's current-model listing but not yet shut down, consistent with that catalog date.
